SPACEPORT IRIDIUM

Console UI — implementation spec

Ten reference screens at 1920×1080 covering every mode, plus the rules that produce them. This is the console variant: navigation lives in a 112px bar welded to the bottom edge, and every heavy screen opens as a left column. The Mode Rail spec documents the vertical-rail alternative — both share the same invariants, palette and type scale, and differ only in where navigation sits.

TARGET 1920×1080 MIN · ONE PANEL AT A TIME · DESKTOP FIRST, CONTROLLER-READY

THE SIX INVARIANTS

01
One panel. Build, Crew, Stores, Trade, R&D, Comms and Overlays are modes, not windows. Opening one closes the last. Two panels can never coexist, so there is no z-order to manage and no “close everything” problem.
02
One inspector. Crew, module, asteroid and corridor selections render into the same bottom-right surface with a swapped tab set. When nothing is selected the surface shrinks to a single line of text rather than vanishing.
03
Left is doing, right is watching. Panels only ever open on the left. Map, alerts and inspector own the right edge permanently and never move, so opening a panel shifts nothing the player was reading.
04
Vitals are pinned; everything else is the ledger. Six resources sit in the console strip; the other twenty-four live behind the ledger chip, grouped Raw ore / Refined / Life support / Goods. Pinning promotes any resource into the strip, so the layout is indifferent to 30 resources or 100.
05
Amber is a budget, not a colour. Cyan means live, selected or affordable. Amber is reserved for breaches, falling vitals and ARC. Nothing decorative is amber, which is why one amber pixel reads instantly.
06
One panel frame. A 56px panel header, a 34px readout header, a 1px #1d2c40 edge, a 1px inner top highlight, and the hotkey right-aligned in the header. Most of the polish gap in the current build is frame inconsistency, not placement.

GEOMETRY

Console112px, full width
Mode button70×74px, 5px gaps
Console zonesmodes 715 / vitals flex / time 247
Panel — Overlays360px
Panel — Build356px + 340px flyout
Panel — Comms620px
Panel — Crew660px
Panel — Stores1080px
Panel — Trade1180px
Panel — R&D1400px
Right column344px, 20px gutter
Inspector420px, bottom-anchored

TYPE

Display / labelsChakra Petch 600–700
Numbers / hotkeysIBM Plex Mono 500–700
Body proseIBM Plex Sans 400–600
Panel title15px, .18em tracking, caps
Readout label11px, .20em tracking, caps
Entity name14–18px Chakra Petch 600
Metric13–16px Mono 700
Meta line10–11px Mono 500, caps
Mode button label9px, .10em tracking, caps
Min on-screen size9px labels, 11px everything else
Neveritalics; no icon fonts in HUD

PALETTE

VOID
#05080e
Play-area base. Nebula is a radial gradient over it, never a texture.
PANEL
#0b111b
Every surface. 0.94–0.98 alpha when it floats over the station.
CONSOLE
#0d1420
Console gradient top; #080d15 bottom. The only surface with a cyan top border.
EDGE
#1d2c40
The only border on inert panels. #16222f for internal dividers.
LIVE
#4fbfd9
Active mode, selection, affordable, positive rate. Glows only on badges and the map viewport.
ATTENTION
#e5a34a
Breach, falling vital, unread transmission, ARC. Budgeted.
GROWTH
#4fbf7a
Built modules, biomass, researched tech. Never a UI state.
DESTRUCTIVE
#d4614f
Demolish and fire. Outline only, never a filled button.
TEXT
#9db9c9
Primary body. #eaf6fb emphasis, #5f7d94 secondary, #4a6d85 meta.

ESC IS ALWAYS AN EXIT
Every panel closes to this frame, so ESC means one thing everywhere: step out one level and eventually land here. Nothing in this state can be dismissed further, which is what makes the key safe to hammer.
ALERTS KEEP A HISTORY
The feed shows the live queue; HISTORY sits beside CLEAR ALL and opens the full log. Clearing is therefore non-destructive, so players will actually use it instead of letting 40 rows pile up.
THE INSPECTOR IS THE ONLY SELECTION SURFACE
Crew here, module in the next screen — same box, same position, different tab set. Nothing about selection changes when a mode panel is open behind it.
PERSISTENT VS SUMMONED
Four things survive with no panel open: how much of everything, where things are, what just happened, and what time it is. Everything else is summoned. That split is the whole layout in one sentence.

TWO STAGE, NOT A DRILLDOWN
The category list never scrolls away, so the player keeps their place and can hop categories without a back step. 696px total, and only while browsing.
SELECTED MODULE EXPLAINS ITSELF
Description and its rate/draw line render inline rather than in a hover tooltip — survives keyboard and controller navigation, and is readable while the ghost is already on the station.
HOLDING STATE LIVES ON THE STATION
Once picked up, the module becomes a ghost under the cursor with its cost and rotate hint attached, so the instruction is where the player is looking.
LOCKED IS VISIBLE, NOT HIDDEN
Un-researched modules stay in the list, dimmed, showing their gating tech. That list is half of what makes R&D legible.

STATUS IS THE PRIMARY COLUMN
“Working at Mining Bay”, “Moving to Refinery”, “Idle” — a full sentence, colour-coded: cyan working, grey transitional, dim idle, amber emergency. Idle is what the player is scanning for.
MORALE IS A BAR, NOT A NUMBER
Bars are comparable at a glance down a column; numbers are not. The number stays for players who want it, and turns amber below 50.
FOOTER STATES THE PROBLEM
A one-line summary — idle count, unhappy count, bunks short — so the panel answers “is my crew fine?” without reading six rows.
SELECTING A ROW USES THE INSPECTOR
Clicking a name fills the same right-hand inspector as clicking the person on the station. One detail view, two ways in.

PRIORITY IS THE POINT
The stepper is the only editable control in the panel and gets the widest hit target. Sign is carried by colour as well as by the number: cyan pulls stock in, amber pushes it away.
CONTENTS ARE CHIPS, NOT A TABLE

AVAIL IS THE COLUMN THAT MATTERS
Held is stock; Avail is what is not reserved. Selling into a reservation is the mistake this table exists to prevent.
DIRECTION COMES FROM THE SIGN
A single stepper per line, positive sells and negative buys, so there are no buy/sell tabs or radio pairs to keep in sync.
SUMMARY, NOT A CART
A 30-line order makes a per-item cart unreadable; the footer carries the line count, the direction split and the running Net beside Clear and Confirm.
READOUTS SURVIVE THE WIDTH
Map and alerts stay mounted — a breach during trading must still be visible. Only the inspector hides, since selection means nothing here.

LEFT TO RIGHT IS THE READING ORDER
Tiers advance rightward and connect with hairlines; the player’s eye starts at what is done and travels toward what is expensive. Vertical trees fight the panel’s shape.
THREE STATES, THREE TREATMENTS
Researched is green-edged, in-progress is cyan and glowing, available is a plain cyan edge, locked is dashed and dimmed. Cost renders in place of the state label when a tech is purchasable.
THE HEADER CARRIES THE BUDGET
RP balance and income live in the panel header, and the current project’s remaining cost and ETA sit in the filter row — the two numbers that decide every click in this panel.
A SECOND TREE IS A TAB
The Engineering / Xenology tabs are where the second currency’s tree lands. No new panel, no new mode — the layout already has the slot.

A MODE, NOT A FLYOUT
Overlays obeys the one-panel rule like everything else, so it can never sit on top of Build. That is the whole reason it is a mode rather than a popover.
THE PANEL CLOSES, THE OVERLAY STAYS

IT TEACHES THE HOTKEYS
Every row prints its number. The panel exists for discoverability and for the mouse, and it makes itself redundant over time rather than replacing the keys.

The panel opens directly above the LEDGER chip and stops short of the right-edge column. Console flyouts never open over the map, alerts or inspector.
FOUR CATEGORIES, FOUR COLUMNS
Raw ore / Refined / Life support / Goods, with amount and per-cycle rate on every line. Thirty resources fit without scrolling; a hundred adds rows, not layout.
PINNING IS THE ESCAPE VALVE
The pin control on each row promotes a resource into the console strip. The player curates their own vitals, which is what keeps the strip from growing with the game.
IT IS NOT A MODE ON PURPOSE
Checking stock mid-build should not close Build. The ledger is the one panel allowed to coexist with a mode — it is a readout, not a workspace.

SUGGESTED BUILD ORDER

01
Extract the shared panel frame first — 56px header, 34px readout header, edge, inner highlight, hotkey slot. Every later step gets cheaper, and this alone closes most of the polish gap.
02
Build the console and make mode mounting exclusive. Port existing screens in behind it unchanged; they will look inconsistent for a while and still behave better than they do now.
03
Collapse the crew and module panels into the single inspector with a swappable tab set, including the nothing-selected line. Asteroid and corridor become two more tab sets on the same surface.
04
Split the resource bar into the pinned strip plus the ledger, with pin state persisted per save. Do this before adding more resources, not after.
05
Convert the top-centre overlay description into the alert feed with its history log, and make Overlays a mode so every overlay is reachable by mouse as well as by number key.
06
Widen-in-place for Trade and R&D, then retire the remaining pop-up windows. Comms, Stores and the system map arrive as console buttons after that, with no layout change.
